contexts.text: The celestial man is His likeness. AC 288. AC 473.
When faith has been conjoined with love, it is then called very good, because the Lord then actuates him as His likeness.
The Most Ancient Church itself, which was celestial, is what is called... The likeness of God ().
Into the likeness of God made He him = that he was made celestial. AC 472.
In this were they likenesses of the Lord; and therefore in perceptive things they became His images.
The universal Heaven is a likeness of the Lord; for the Lord is all in all things of them. Each Society is also a likeness; thus each Angel...
In love to the Lord there is the nearest image of the Lord, which is called a likeness; and therefore those who are in love to the Lord itself are called His likenesses.
The Inmost Heaven, being nearest the Lord, is called His likeness.
Agreement, or likeness, conjoins.
Hence Heaven is a likeness and image of the Lord.
The Angels who appear thus are likenesses of the Lord. Described.

In spiritual and celestial things... it is a state of similitude which makes approach and presence; and it is the love which makes similitude and dissimilitude. AC 9579. AC 9968. AC 10130:3. HH 42:end. HH 193. AE 628.
This makes the likeness of the man to a brute animal.
(Thou shalt not make to thyself) any likeness () = a resemblance of those things which are from the Divine. Explained. AC 8871. AC 8872.
In the angelic Societies they love, recognize, and consociate with each other according to the similitudes and proximities of goods.
Hence the body is the likeness of its soul... Hence it is that men are born in the likeness of their fathers. (Compare NJHD 287.)
(For) the good which proceeds from the Lord is a likeness of Him, because He is in it; and those become likenesses of Him... who make good and truth to be of their life...
Likenesses in general, and variations in particular. Explained.

That which reigns inflows into each thing... and everywhere induces a likeness of itself. In the Heavens love to the Lord is regnant... Hence the Lord... inflows into all and each... and puts on them a likeness of Himself. HH 72.
Every Society of Heaven... is in the likeness of a man.
In the most perfect form... there is a likeness of the parts with the whole... HH 73.

Among those who are in a like evil, and thence in a like infernal Society, there is a general likeness; from which as from a plane of derivation the faces of all there appear to have a certain likeness.
That there is such a likeness of both worlds. References.
Part of the truths of the sense of the letter... are like similitudes and comparisons...
For similitude conjoins them.
The perfection of the created universe is from the similitude of the generals and the particulars. Explained.

For as to affections there is a likeness of nations to their first progenitor; and a greater likeness in families; and a still greater likeness in houses. Nay, there is such a likeness that (they) are distinguishable not only by their minds, but also by their faces.
By the image of God () is meant the Divine wisdom; and by the likeness of God, the Divine love; for wisdom is nothing else than the image of love...
The image and likeness of the Lord is in (men) from creation; the image in them is wisdom, and the likeness in them is love...
(The cause of the likeness in families, etc. Explained.)
The likenesses of the locusts () = the appearances and images of those who have confirmed with themselves faith separated from charity.
In the Spiritual World... two cannot dwell together in the same house unless they are similitudes...
(A discussion there as to) what is the image of God, and what the likeness of God, into which man was created. See fully stated under Image.
That with consorts there are various similitudes and various dissimilitudes, both internal and external. (Explained.)
In general the similitudes and dissimilitudes originate from connate inclinations, varied by education, the company which is kept, and the persuasions which have been imbued.
That various similitudes can be conjoined; but not with dissimilitudes. Explained.
That the Lord provides similitudes for those who long for love truly conjugial; and that if they are not given on earth, He provides them in the Heavens. (Explained.)
The Lord (then) opens the internal similitudes.
This is Known from the likeness of the inclinations and affections.
Internal similitudes and dissimilitudes originate solely from religion; for this is implanted in souls...
Whereas external similitudes and dissimilitudes are not of souls, but of lower minds. Explained.
Therefore (in the Spiritual World) similitudes are conjoined, and dissimilitudes are separated.
The similitude (of the internal affections) is not seen in the woman...
Because the choice of internal similitudes cannot be provided by the Lord on earth as in the Heavens...
The animals (there) are likenesses of the affections of love and the derivative thoughts of the Angels.
The body... may be made either to the likeness of the father, or to the likeness of the mother; the image of the father still remaining within the latter...
This may be illustrated by various similitudes. TCR 119:2.

Sympathies and antipathies are nothing else than exhalations of affections from minds, which affect the other according to the similitudes, and cause aversion according to the dissimilitudes. These, although innumerable, and unperceived by any sense of the body, are yet perceived by the sense of the soul as one; and according to them are effected all conjunctions and consociations in the Spiritual World. SE 980.
They put on a likeness of the ideas of another.

In the other life friendships and intimacies are not made by intercourse; but similitudes of lower minds effect such things; and therefore when anyone appears he is at once Known either as a friend or as an enemy, from the similitude or dissimilitude. Explained.
A likeness and an analogy...

The likeness of God, according to which man has been made, is that he can live in all appearance as of himself; consequently that he can receive from God the things which are of love and the things which are of wisdom, and can reproduce them in a likeness as God [does] of Himself; for God says: Behold the man was as one of us, in knowing good and evil. Explained. Coro 29.
The likeness of God is this free determination.
